plan.contextChunk: This figure is a schematic of a single array drawn as a long horizontal strip of equal cells, shaded to mark off four regions. Four italic labels sit above the strip: p over the leftmost cell, i over the fourth cell, j further to the right, and r over the rightmost cell. Three heavy black bars stand between cells as the region boundaries. The four cells from p through i are pale gray; the six cells between the first and second bar are a darker gray; the five cells after the second bar and before the last are white and empty; and the single cell at the right end, under r, is white and holds the italic letter x. Three curly braces beneath the strip label the pale gray stretch as at most x, written with the symbol for less than or equal to followed by x, the dark gray stretch as greater than x, and the white stretch as unrestricted. The shading separates the portion of the array already classified against the pivot from the portion not yet examined. The strip states the invariant holding at the top of each iteration while a subarray is rearranged in place around the pivot value stored at position r.

interactionPlan.concept: The partition algorithm maintains a loop invariant by growing a 'less than or equal to pivot' region and a 'greater than pivot' region step-by-step as it scans the array.
elements: Horizontal array of cells representing array A
Pointer label 'p' over the first cell
Pointer label 'i' over the current last element of the <= x region
Pointer label 'j' over the first element of the unrestricted region
Pointer label 'r' over the last cell
Label 'x' inside the cell at index r, representing the pivot value
Thick black vertical bar separating the <= x and > x regions (between index i and i+1)
Thick black vertical bar separating the > x and unrestricted regions (between index j-1 and j)
Thick black vertical bar separating the unrestricted region and the pivot (between index r-1 and r)
Pale gray shading for cells from p to i
Dark gray shading for cells from i+1 to j-1
White background for cells from j to r-1
Curly brace below cells p..i labeled '≤ x'
Curly brace below cells i+1..j-1 labeled '> x'
Curly brace below cells j..r-1 labeled 'unrestricted'

interactions.label: Partition Algorithm
interactions.teaches: How the i and j pointers divide the array into four distinct regions, and how examining A[j] determines whether the > x region grows or the <= x region grows.

api.does: exchanges elements at idx1 and idx2 in the array
moves pointer i and updates the right boundary of the pale gray <= x region
moves pointer j and updates the left boundary of the unrestricted region

interactions.frame: The array A populated with values, pointers p, i, j, r, region shading (pale gray, dark gray, white), thick dividers, and bottom braces — all updated dynamically to reflect the current indices i and j.
interactions.success_check: All elements to the left of the returned pivot index are <= the pivot, and all elements to the right are > the pivot.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: By advancing j, every element is evaluated against the pivot and swapped into the correct region, leaving the invariant intact until the entire array is partitioned.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Draw a horizontal row of contiguous square cells. Position italicized pointer labels p, i, j, r above the cells. Place thick black vertical bars between cells to demarcate regions: after index i, before index j, and before index r. The region from p to i is pale gray; i+1 to j-1 is dark gray; j to r-1 is white. Cell r contains 'x' and is white. Draw curly braces underneath each of the three main regions with their respective labels ('≤ x', '> x', 'unrestricted'). Dynamically update the shading, bars, and braces as the i and j pointers are modified by the API.

plan.authoredInteractions:
- Code editor for PARTITION(A, p, r): learner implements the loop using pivot x, indices i and j, compare(A[j], x), and swap primitives; each executed line advances the strip boundaries and updates the <= x, > x, and unrestricted regions.
- Step-through invariant view: before and after every loop iteration, the diagram highlights which cells satisfy the invariant A[p..i] <= x, A[i+1..j-1] > x, and A[j..r-1] unrestricted.
- Test-case toggle: switch the current A[j] between <= x and > x cases to see why one branch swaps and advances i while the other only advances j.

discrepancies: The default view shows the initialization step where the '≤ x' and '> x' regions are empty and their braces are collapsed, whereas the source figure illustrates an intermediate step with all three regions populated and clearly visible.

The generated figure populates the array with concrete numbers and places a small 'x' in the corner of the pivot cell, while the source figure uses abstract empty boxes with a large centered 'x' for the pivot.
Variable labels (p, j, i) are stacked vertically at the left edge of the array in the default initial state, instead of being distributed across the regions as shown in the source.
evaluation.notes: An exceptionally well-designed interactive simulation of the partition algorithm; however, because it defaults to the t=0 initialization state, it visually misses the classic three-region intermediate layout that defines the source figure.
action_items: Initialize `currentFrameIdx` to an intermediate frame (e.g., `Math.floor((currentFrames.length - 1) / 2)`) instead of `0` inside `handleWorkerResult()` so the default view displays all three regions and braces, matching the source.
Center the 'x' text in the pivot cell and consider hiding the numeric value for that specific cell to better match the abstract visual emphasis of the source figure.
